findings.title: The §15.11 intermediate states after steps 3 and 4 are not green, and the state after step 4 permanently destroys invalidation signal on any real database it touches
findings.plan_sections: §13 steps 3–5; §15.11 all three bullets; §15.8 items 2 and 4
findings.claim: §15.11 claims each intermediate state is shippable-green. Neither the state after step 3 nor the state after step 4 is. Step 3 (§13) says `write_answer` is replaced by `on_answer` and `inv_fields` is dropped, but the gate that would supply version/interpreted_at is only built in step 5 — so after step 3 there is no channel at all from the (still unchanged) scan to the write, and §15.11's own description of that state ("every answer is written at once with the scan's fields") is unimplementable as written. Worse, after step 4 the scan no longer mints (§15.8 item 2 removes `counter_next`) while the gate that mints instead does not exist yet. §15.11 says the consequence is only that "a changed definition's dependents are re-interpreted only on the next run". That is wrong: the entity is re-interpreted and its record is rewritten with the NEW digest and the OLD version, so on the next run its digest matches, its version never rose, eff* never rises, and its dependents are never re-interpreted — ever. The signal is not deferred, it is destroyed, silently, in whatever database the developer runs against between steps 4 and 5.
findings.evidence: Today the mint is the scan's, in one write transaction: semantic_interpretation.py:939-962 (`v = Semantic_DB.counter_next(txn)` at :954, `txn.put(...version=v)` at :955-957), and it reaches the write only through `version_to_write` → `inv_fields` (semantic_interpretation.py:1177-1178) → `InterpretationTask.write_answer` (:381-402, `version, interpreted_at = self.inv_fields[task_idx]` at :390). Removing `inv_fields` (§13 step 3) and the scan's mint (§13 step 4) before `_write` exists (§13 step 5) leaves `version=None`/`interpreted_at=None` on every write; `write_answer`'s own `tracked = version is not None` test (:392) then also blanks `semantic_digest` and `deps`. Any run performed in that window rewrites live records in the user's `~/.cache/Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding` store.
findings.proposed_fix: Two changes. (a) Keep `inv_fields` and `write_answer` alive through steps 3 and 4 and delete them only in step 5, and say so in §13 step 3 instead of "inv_fields dropped". (b) Merge §13 steps 4 and 5 into one step (scan rewrite + gate together), because the scan's mint and the gate's mint are one mechanism split across two commits; the write path must never be without exactly one of them. If they must stay separate, §15.11 must state explicitly that the post-step-4 tree may not be run against any store the developer cares about (and must correct the false claim that dependents are merely deferred to the next run).

findings.title: test_incremental_criteria.py asserts exactly the scan behaviour step 4 removes, and neither §10 nor §15.10 mentions the file
findings.claim: §15.10 maps §10's tests onto four files (test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py, test_interpretation_driver.py, test_interpretation_mcp_server.py, a new test_semantic_change_gate.py). `test_incremental_criteria.py` is not among them, yet it is the file that pins the current scan, and three of its assertions become false the moment step 4 lands: the scan re-stamping the wire digest, the scan bumping the version, and a digest change on A pulling its dependent B in through the closure. Under D13 the last one is now *intended* to be false (only A is a seed), so the file cannot simply be "kept green" — it has to be rewritten, and the plan gives no instruction to do so. As it stands the implementer meets three red tests at step 4 with nothing telling them whether they are a regression or the design.
findings.evidence: test_incremental_criteria.py:121 `assert r.semantic_digest == DG_A, "the scan re-stamps the wire digest"`; :122 `assert r.version is not None and r.version > 1, "a genuine change bumps"`; :124-125 `assert _dry(entries) == 2  # stable` and `assert _rec("a").version == v_after` — all three depend on semantic_interpretation.py:953-960. test_incremental_criteria.py:135 `assert _dry(entries) == 2, "corrupting only a must pull b in through its dep edge (eff)"` — under the new seed rule b is not a seed (a's record still looks fresh because nothing minted), so the answer becomes 1, which is precisely §5.2's "Why no closure" paragraph and §10's "only A is a seed" bullet.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `archive/tests/test_incremental_criteria.py` to §15.10's mapping with the three concrete edits: delete the re-stamp/bump assertions from `test_fresh_record_leaves_and_digest_mismatch_reenters` (they become "the scan writes nothing": assert the record is byte-identical after `_dry`), and convert `test_eff_propagates_through_the_dep_edge` into §10's enrolment test — `_dry` returns 1 (only A seeded) and the live run interprets B only after A's CHANGED verdict. Do this in the same commit as step 4 so the suite is never red for a reason nobody wrote down.

findings.title: Wrapping the run in an asyncio.TaskGroup changes the exception interpret_file raises, and nothing in §10 pins the raised type
findings.plan_sections: §5.4 ("one asyncio task per entity in an asyncio.TaskGroup owned by interpret_file"); §15.1 (`interpret_file`: "scan, task group, closing line"); §10 (failure bullets)
findings.claim: `asyncio.TaskGroup.__aexit__` wraps *any* exception that leaves its body — including one the body raised with no child failing at all — in an `ExceptionGroup`. Once `_run_agent` and the completeness backstop run inside the group, `interpret_file` stops raising `FatalAgentError` and starts raising `ExceptionGroup('unhandled errors in a TaskGroup', [FatalAgentError(...)])`. `str(e)` then no longer begins with `USER_ERROR_MARKER`, and any `except FatalAgentError` a caller adds later silently stops matching. §10's failure bullets test the gate's verdicts and that "`GateError` fails the run", but nothing asserts what type and what message reach the RPC boundary.
findings.evidence: Measured on this machine's interpreter (Python 3.12.3): `async with asyncio.TaskGroup(): raise E('[MARKER] boom')` → `ExceptionGroup('unhandled errors in a TaskGroup', [E('[MARKER] boom')])`. The two raise sites that move inside the group are semantic_interpretation.py:1244 (the completeness backstop `raise FatalAgentError(_msg_unanswered(...))`) and `_run_agent`'s re-raises at :837 and :849. The ML side reads the message by substring: Tools/semantic_store.ML:1434-1440 `extract_user_error` / :1442-1445 `interpretation_rpc_error`. It survives today only because rpc.py:344 uses `traceback.format_exception(e)`, which happens to render sub-exception text — i.e. the human-readable-error contract now rests on a traceback formatting accident.
findings.proposed_fix: Either (a) do not use a bare `async with TaskGroup` around the session: run `_run_agent` as a member task of the group and re-raise the single non-`GateError` cause, or (b) wrap the group in `except* FatalAgentError`/`except BaseExceptionGroup` in `interpret_file` and re-raise the first leaf. Whichever is chosen, add to §10: "a `FatalAgentError` raised by the session (stalled retries) leaves `interpret_file` as a `FatalAgentError` whose `str()` starts with `USER_ERROR_MARKER`, not as an `ExceptionGroup`", and the same for `GateError`.

findings.title: Moving the statement refresh behind the LLM loop means a pure `expr` change is never refreshed at all, because n = 0 short-circuits the live run
findings.plan_sections: §5.3.2 ("Today's scan-time refresh moved after the LLM work; after the dry-run early return"); §13 step 4; §15.8 item 8; §10 bullet "statement refresh; dry run returns the seed count"
findings.claim: Today the `expr` refresh happens inside the scan, so it runs on a dry run too. §5.3.2 moves it after the loop and after the dry-run early return. But `update_interpretations` returns immediately when the dry-run count is 0, so for a theory whose only difference is a changed printed statement — no digest change, no dep change, nothing stale — the seed set is empty, the quote is 0, the live run is never started, and `update_expr` is never called. The stored `expr` stays stale forever and, because `update_expr` is what invalidates the vector, the embedding keeps describing text the entity no longer has. This bites persistent-theory entries hardest: they carry no digest and no deps, so the refresh is their *only* update path.
findings.evidence: Scan-time refresh today: semantic_interpretation.py:1128-1129 (`if e.prop_str and rec.expr != e.prop_str: Semantic_DB.update_expr(...)`), inside the phase-3 loop that also runs under `dry_run` (the dry-run return is at :1136-1143, after it). The short-circuit: semantics.py:1844-1845 `if n == 0: return` in `update_interpretations`, and the same guard exists at Tools/interpret_command.ML:122 per §5.2. `update_expr` invalidating the vector is pinned by test_layered_db.py:580-591.
findings.proposed_fix: Either keep the statement refresh in the scan (it writes no gate field and mints nothing, so it does not violate §6.3's "the scan and a dry run write nothing" beyond an already-existing exception — say so explicitly in §11's discipline-3 rewrite), or count `expr`-only differences into the seed set so n > 0 pulls the theory into the live run. Add to §10: "a theory whose only change is `prop_str` — dry run returns 0 — still ends with the stored `expr` refreshed and the vector invalidated."

findings.title: §15.8 contradicts itself about the ε reading for a version-less record; the choice it spells out in code silently makes such records permanently fresh and breaks test_eff_star's reference cross-check
findings.plan_sections: §15.8 items 2 and 4; §10 bullet "eff*: ported verification assertions ... None/ε/missing cases"
findings.claim: §15.8 item 2 says the scan "keeps computing, per entry, ... the ε reading for a version-less record" and then, in the same sentence, that "the scan needs no counter at all". Item 4 settles it in code as `_EffStar.eff_value(rec.version or 0, e.deps)`. Reading a stored `version` of None/0 as 0 rather than as ε changes the verdict: a record that has a matching digest but no version has eff* = 0 and `interpreted_at` = 0, so `0 > 0` is false — it is not a seed, it is never re-interpreted, and it never acquires a version. Today it is stale by construction (`version_to_write[i] = epsilon` at semantic_interpretation.py:951/962, then `eff_v > 0` at :1122-1124). This is a behaviour change nobody decided, and it is not on §10's list.
findings.evidence: semantic_interpretation.py:940 `epsilon = Semantic_DB.counter_value(txn)`, :946-951 and :962 assign `epsilon` as the entity's own version for the eff walk, consumed at :1122 `eff_value(version_to_write.get(i, rec.version or 0), e.deps)` and :1131. The reference cross-check encodes exactly that rule: test_eff_star.py:139-140 `own = r.version or epsilon` / `eff_entity(by_key, own, r.deps, shielded=True)`, driven over `_random_store`'s `version=rng.choice([None, 0, ...])` (test_eff_star.py:113) by `test_production_scan_agrees_with_the_reference_on_random_stores` (:145-163). With `rec.version or 0` that test fails on the first seed producing a version-None record.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide in §15.8 which reading stands, in one sentence, and make items 2 and 4 agree. If ε stays (the conservative reading, and the one that matches D10's "an outcome the gate could not judge is CHANGED"), the scan still needs one read-only `counter_value` and item 4 becomes `eff_value(rec.version or epsilon, e.deps)`; test_eff_star.py needs no change. If 0 is intended, §15.10 must list test_eff_star.py as a file to update (`_expected_stale`'s `own`) and §10 must gain a bullet stating that a digest-carrying record with no version is now treated as fresh.

findings.title: §15.10 claims the existing driver-suite scenarios keep their assertions, but D14 deletes the write the central one is about, and both harness hooks it uses cease to exist
findings.claim: §15.10 lists six scenarios that "keep their assertions", including "a failed write is not counted". Under D14 the answer path performs no database write at all — `on_answer` records the text in memory and starts a gate — so that scenario has nothing left to fail, and the invariant it was written to defend ("answered means durable") is deliberately retired. The two hooks the whole harness hangs on also disappear: `_RecordingTask` overrides `write_answer`, and `test_interpretation_mcp_server.py` imports the module-level `_answer_tool` and asserts on `task.written`. §15.10 mentions only the batch-handoff reply text for the MCP file.
findings.evidence: The retired invariant is written into the code as a load-bearing comment: semantic_interpretation.py:602-608 ("PERSIST FIRST, MARK IN MEMORY SECOND ... This way 'answered' means 'durable'") with the per-item guard at :614-623. Its test is test_interpretation_driver.py:172-209, which monkeypatches `task.write_answer` (:184-189) and asserts `task.written == [...]` (:201) and "the entry whose write failed must stay unanswered" (:202-203). The harness hook is test_interpretation_driver.py:48-49 (`def write_answer(self, task_idx, sem): self.written.append(...)`). The MCP file imports `_answer_tool` at test_interpretation_mcp_server.py:23 and asserts `task.written == [(0, "the zeroth"), (1, "the first")]` at :114.
findings.proposed_fix: In §15.10 replace "a failed write is not counted" with its D14 successor and name the harness changes: `_RecordingTask` records `on_answer` calls instead of `write_answer`, the failure scenario becomes "a gate whose write raises fails the run with `GateError` and the entity is not counted as interpreted" (moved to the new test_semantic_change_gate.py, since it now needs a task group), and test_interpretation_mcp_server.py's `_answer_tool` import becomes `mk_answer_tool(task)` with `task.written` replaced by the recorded `on_answer` calls. Also state explicitly in §11 that the comment at semantic_interpretation.py:602-608 must be rewritten, or the file will carry a comment asserting the opposite of what the code does.

findings.title: §10's concurrency bullet does not say how gates are made to actually overlap, and with an obvious fake judge they never will
findings.plan_sections: §10 bullet "concurrency: several gates in flight at once (no limit) write correct, distinct records; each judge session receives exactly one entity"; §15.5 ("Between a gate's `await` points another gate may write; that is the intended semantics"); §15.10 (new test file uses "a fake judge driver (scripted verdicts)")
findings.claim: The only thing that makes concurrency observable in this design is that a gate yields at `_prefilter` and `_judge`. A fake judge driver written the natural way (an async function that returns a scripted verdict without awaiting anything that suspends) never yields, so every gate runs to completion inside its own `create_task` step and the gates are serialised — the test passes without ever exercising the interleaving it names. That hides the failure modes that only appear when two gates overlap: a gate reading `rec_cache` between another gate's `_write` and its `_propagate`, a mint landing between a gate's `_judge` and its `eff_star`, and a `_DONE` snapshot raise racing a sibling's write.
findings.evidence: §15.5's `_gate` yields only at `await _prefilter(...)` and `await _judge(...)`; everything from `_write` through `_propagate` is synchronous by design ("the LMDB writes are synchronous blocks with no `await` inside"). The scenario the plan itself calls out as order-sensitive is §5.3.1's third bullet (a dependent already `_DONE` when its dependency mints) versus the second (`gating` → "its write comes later and its snapshot will include the mint") — which of the two fires depends entirely on the relative order of two gates' await points.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the overlap explicit in §10: the fake judge driver must block on a per-entity `asyncio.Event` the test releases in a chosen order, and the concurrency test must assert both orderings of a dependency/dependent pair — A's verdict before B's write (B's own snapshot absorbs the mint, no `update_gate_fields` call) and B's write before A's verdict (B is `_DONE`, the snapshot raise fires exactly once, B's own dependents are not enrolled). Assert the number of `update_gate_fields` calls, not just the final `interpreted_at`, so a run that happened to serialise cannot pass for a run that interleaved.

findings.title: §15.10's `_make_task` mutates the module global `_BATCH_SIZE` with a fixture that cannot reach the two other files importing it
findings.plan_sections: §15.10 second bullet ("`_make_task(n, batch_size)` builds a task with every entry enrolled and sets `SI._BATCH_SIZE` for the test (restored by an autouse fixture)")
findings.claim: Today `_make_task` takes `batch_size` and slices the batches itself, touching no global. §15.10 makes it write `SI._BATCH_SIZE` and relies on an autouse fixture to restore it. An autouse fixture declared in test_interpretation_driver.py applies only to tests collected from that module; `_make_task` is imported and called from two other modules, and there is no conftest.py anywhere in the tree to hold a shared fixture. Those modules' calls would leave `_BATCH_SIZE` permanently changed for the rest of the pytest session, making later tests order-dependent — the exact failure class the repo already fought once (test_incremental_criteria.py:30-36 documents a measured cross-file leak of `SEMANTIC_DB_DIR`).
findings.evidence: `_make_task(n, batch_size)` today: test_interpretation_driver.py:71-77, batching locally with no global write. Cross-module importers: test_interpretation_codex.py:48 `from test_interpretation_driver import _make_task` (used at :126, :139, :153, :161, :173, :197, :290, :300, :325, :333) and test_interpretation_mcp_server.py:25 (used at :85, :120, :133, :149). `ls conftest.py ../conftest.py ../../conftest.py` from archive/tests reports no such file at any level. The prior leak is documented at test_incremental_criteria.py:30-36.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not put the batch size in a module global for the tests to patch. Make it an `AgentTask` attribute (`self.batch_size = _BATCH_SIZE`) that `next_batch` reads — `InterpretationTask` then takes it as a constructor argument, `JudgeTask` sets it to 1, and `_make_task(n, batch_size)` keeps its present signature with no global mutation and no fixture at all. That also removes the last reason `_BATCH_SIZE` has to be reachable from outside the module.

accurate: The gate's storage layer and its test file are in good shape and need nothing from this lens: `archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py` already pins the 15-field codec against legacy 12/13/14-field arities in both writers, the creation-from-absent and tombstone-resurrection shapes, the "aborted write leaves store and counter byte-identical" crash shape (ii), the vector-invalidation asymmetry between `update_interpretation` and `gate_write`, and the raw-put grant assert in both directions — so §15.10's step-3 addition (`put_interpretation`) drops into an existing, well-shaped harness with an obvious template. §10's list is genuinely thorough where it counts: it names the enrolment cases D13 actually turns on (only A seeded, C enrolled only after B's CHANGED, nothing after UNCHANGED, an enrolment arriving after the queue emptied), the snapshot raise with its two negative halves (B not re-interpreted, B's own dependents not enrolled through the raise), the recycle scenario with a partially answered batch, the rec_cache write-back wall, the prefilter's scale invariance and zero-norm case, `JudgeTask` cannot write, and the non-LLM regression against `pairs_phase2.json` — that is the right set of failure modes for the queue, the per-entity gate and the corrections. The eff\* work of step 2 is already landed and cross-checked two ways (the shape assertions of `test_eff_star.py:25-91` plus 150 random stores against the independent condensation reference in `eff_reference.py`), which is the strongest evidence in the plan that §4 is right; §13's decision to land the Record field and eff\* first, before any behaviour change, was the right first two steps. §15.5's observation that every LMDB write sits in a synchronous block with no `await` inside is the correct load-bearing argument for why concurrent gates cannot interleave inside a transaction, and §15.4's wait-for-progress reasoning (a set between `next_batch` and `wait` is not lost because the event stays set until cleared) is sound as written.

findings.title: Derived permissions are applied to `allowed_tools` only; the PreToolUse hook is the actual enforcement and would deny every MCP tool
findings.claim: §5.5 says `_TOOL_WHITELIST` shrinks to the CLI built-ins, `_permission_control` becomes a closure inside `_options()`, and `allowed_tools` is derived from `self.tools`. It never says what the closure checks against. In the code the SAME set feeds two consumers: `allowed_tools=list(_TOOL_WHITELIST)` (claude_code.py:453) AND the PreToolUse deny hook `if tool_name not in _TOOL_WHITELIST: return _deny(...)` (claude_code.py:106-108). The hook is the hard enforcement (`permission_mode="default"`). Implemented literally — whitelist shrunk to built-ins, hook still testing membership in it — every call to `mcp__isabelle_semantics__answer` / `query` / `hover` / `definition` / `desugar_and_explain` is denied, and the same for the judge's `mcp__isabelle_semantics__verdict`.
findings.evidence: claude_code.py:61-85 (`_TOOL_WHITELIST` contains both the built-ins and the five `mcp__isabelle_semantics__*` names), :99-111 (`_permission_control` denies anything outside it), :453 (`allowed_tools=list(_TOOL_WHITELIST)`), :465-468 (the hook is registered for matcher `*`). Plan §5.5: "`_TOOL_WHITELIST` shrinks to the CLI built-ins; `_permission_control` becomes a closure inside `_options()`; `allowed_tools` = `mcp__<SERVER_NAME>__<t.name>` for `t in self.tools` plus the built-ins iff `cli_tools`."
findings.proposed_fix: State the invariant structurally rather than as two parallel derivations: give `ClaudeCodeDriver` one method, e.g. `def _allowed_tool_names(self) -> set[str]: return {f"mcp__{SERVER_NAME}__{t.name}" for t in self.tools} | (_CLI_BUILTINS if self.cli_tools else set())`, call it ONCE at the top of `_options()`, and use that one local for both `allowed_tools=sorted(allowed)` and the hook's membership test (the closure captures `allowed`). Rename `_TOOL_WHITELIST` to `_CLI_BUILTINS` so nothing can read as "the whole allowed set" again. Then the option and the hook cannot disagree, which is the property the plan is after ("permissions are derived, never listed").

findings.title: One Codex judge session per entity, unbounded: each is a `codex app-server` subprocess plus its own HTTP MCP session
findings.claim: D12 fixes one judge session per entity with no concurrency limit, and §5.4 starts the gate the moment an answer arrives. On the Codex backend each judge session is not a cheap API call: `CodexDriver.__aenter__` allocates an MCP session id, starts a `_ManagedMCPApp` (an anyio task group + StreamableHTTP session manager) on the process-wide server, constructs `AsyncCodex()` — which spawns a `codex app-server` subprocess — starts a thread, and then blocks on a tool-registration health check with a 30 s timeout. The `answer` tool can submit a whole batch at once, and `_BATCH_SIZE` is 20, so twenty judge sessions can be created in one tool call; `schedule_dag` runs several theories concurrently, multiplying that again. On a transient failure `_run_agent` recycles up to `_MAX_AGENT_RECYCLES = 8` times, each recycle another subprocess. Nothing in the plan bounds this.
findings.evidence: codex.py:224-263 (`__aenter__`: `register_session` + `AsyncCodex()` + `thread_start`), :279-313 (`_check_tools_registered`, `_HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0` at :60), mcp_server.py:146-178 (`_ManagedMCPApp` holds a background task per session), :250-261 (`register_session`), :187-198 (`_SessionRouter` scans its session dict linearly per request); semantic_interpretation.py:135 (`_BATCH_SIZE = 20`), :156 (`_MAX_AGENT_RECYCLES = 8`). Plan D12: "there is no limit on how many judge sessions run at once".
findings.proposed_fix: SPEC RELAXATION of D12's "no limit" (D12's substance — one entity per judge session, in a fresh session, started when the answer arrives — is untouched): add a module-level `_JUDGE_SESSIONS = asyncio.Semaphore(_MAX_CONCURRENT_JUDGES)` held only around `_judge`'s `_run_agent` call, not around the gate task. Concrete gain: the queue keeps flowing and every gate still starts immediately, but the number of live `codex app-server` subprocesses, MCP sessions and open sockets is bounded by one constant instead of by `_BATCH_SIZE` × the number of concurrent theories; the same bound also caps the recycle storm. If even that is unwanted, the plan should at least state the expected peak session count and say that it was checked against Codex's app-server footprint.

findings.title: `on_answer` has no `_NOT_ENROLLED` guard, and §15.8 widens `task.results` to every entry — today's "Unknown entry" protection disappears
findings.claim: Today the task holds only the `uncached` sub-list, so an `answer` for any other entity of the theory is rejected with `Unknown entry` (semantic_interpretation.py:592-593). §15.8 step 7 puts ALL of the theory's entries into the task (so non-seeds can be enrolled later), with `results` prefilled from the store. The `on_answer` pseudo-code in §15.3 branches only on `_DONE` and `_GATING`; an entry in state `_NOT_ENROLLED` falls through to `state = _GATING; start_gate(idx)`. So a label the model emits for an entity this run never sent it — a plausible mistake, since the agent can see neighbouring entity names through the `query` / `hover` / `definition` tools — silently overwrites a good stored interpretation with text produced for a different entity, spends a judge session on it, can mint a version, and counts in `n_interpreted`.
findings.evidence: semantic_interpretation.py:585-593 (`key not in task.results` → `Unknown entry`), :299-347 (`results` is built from whatever `entries` the task was given), :1173-1179 (today: `entries=[entries[i] for i in uncached]`). Plan §15.8 step 7: "over ALL of the theory's entries (not today's `uncached` sub-list)"; §15.3's `on_answer` listing.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the state, not the dict membership, the addressability test: in `on_answer`, `if self.state[idx] == _NOT_ENROLLED: return "not asked"` and have `mk_answer_tool` push that into the handler's existing `errors` list with the same wording shape as today (`Unknown entry: ...` / `Entry not requested: ...`). That keeps the D11 correction path (`_DONE`) and the in-flight path (`_GATING`) exactly as specified while restoring the guard that the widened `results` map removes.

findings.title: A judge driver that cannot even be constructed degrades every gate to CHANGED with host-log-only reporting
findings.claim: §5.4 and §15.5 resolve a judge session that ends in `FatalAgentError` to CHANGED and log it to the host log only. But `FatalAgentError` is also what the drivers raise for CONFIGURATION errors before any turn runs: DeepSeek with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` unset, DeepSeek/Codex with no curated pricing or context window, Claude Code with no CLI on PATH. Those failures are deterministic and affect EVERY gate, so the whole feature silently reverts to today's behaviour (every entity mints, full propagation, every judge session's start-up cost paid) while the run reports success and the user sees nothing. This is asymmetric with the prefilter, whose unavailability does get a user-visible line (§12 #4, #5), and it sits badly with D10's "nothing ever hides a failure".
findings.evidence: deep_seek.py:136-140 (missing API key → `FatalAgentError` from `__init__`), :166-176 (missing pricing / context window), codex.py:214-217 (missing pricing), claude_code.py:479-486 (`CLINotFoundError` → `FatalAgentError` in `__aenter__`); semantic_interpretation.py:842-849 (`_run_agent` re-raises `FatalAgentError` without recycling). Plan §5.4: "a judge session that ends in `FatalAgentError`, or gives no verdict, resolves CHANGED ... and is written to the **host log only**"; §12: "Host-log only (never shown): judge session failed".
findings.proposed_fix: Distinguish "this judge session failed" from "the judge backend is unusable": keep host-log-only for a per-session failure, but the FIRST `FatalAgentError` raised before the judge's first turn (driver construction / `__aenter__`) sets a run flag and prints one user-visible line, in the shape of §12 #5, e.g. `[Semantic_Embedding] The judge backend could not start: <error>; every entity is treated as changed for the rest of this run.` One flag, one line per run, no new decision — the verdict stays CHANGED as D10 requires. The wording is user-visible, so it needs the owner's approval.

findings.plan_sections: §15.5 (`_write`, plan lines 933-939); §5.4 step 5 ("rec_cache == store" holds for every later eff*, lines 289-291); §6.3 counter invariant
findings.claim: `_write` inserts a provisional record carrying the minted version into `task.rec_cache` *before* `put_interpretation`, and only overwrites it with the committed record after the `with` block. If anything inside the transaction raises (the two blockers above, an encoding error, `MapFullError`), LMDB rolls back both the record and the counter bump, but `rec_cache` keeps the phantom version. §5.4 step 5's stated invariant ("on commit the record is put back into rec_cache, so 'rec_cache == store' holds for every later eff*") is then false, and any later eff* over that cache can compute an `interpreted_at` above the counter — the one value §6.3 says must never be stored. That it is not exploitable today rests on an unstated asyncio detail (a sibling gate suspended at an await is cancelled by the TaskGroup before it can reach its own synchronous `_write`), which is precisely an invariant kept by remembering rather than by shape.
findings.evidence: Plan §15.5, ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:933 (`task.rec_cache[e.universal_key] = provisional record with the new version`) inside the `with Semantic_DB.gate_write() as w:` block opened at line 921, versus line 939 (`task.rec_cache[e.universal_key] = written`) after it; §5.4 step 5 at lines 289-291. The rollback semantics are LMDB's: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:970-977 (`gate_write` yields inside `env.begin(write=True)`) and the mint's same-transaction rule at semantics.py:559-568. §6.3's invariant is stated at plan line 419.
findings.proposed_fix: Never mutate shared state before the commit: give `_EffStar.eff_value` an `overlay` parameter (`{key: provisional}`) used only for this one call, and assign `task.rec_cache[key] = written` solely after the transaction commits. If the overlay is judged too much machinery, wrap the block in `try/except` that restores `task.rec_cache[key] = rec` before re-raising as `GateError`, and state the restore as part of §5.4 step 5.

findings.title: `put_interpretation` inside `Gate_Writer` breaks the class's raw-put grant, the invariant the existing tests pin
findings.claim: `Gate_Writer` exists as "raw puts under the grant: no vector is invalidated", and `gate_write()` enforces that by asserting `_GATE_FIELDS ∩ _EMBEDDED_DOC_FIELDS = ∅` once per transaction. Step 3 adds `put_interpretation` to that same class — a put that writes `kind`, `name`, `expr` and `interpretation`, all four of them embedded-document fields, and that invalidates vectors itself. After the change the class-level assertion no longer describes the class: it guards one of the two puts and is decorative for the other, so a future field added to `put_interpretation`'s signature is checked by nothing. §15.7 already introduces the shared `_put_fields` helper but leaves the invalidation decision with each caller.
findings.evidence: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:936-938 (class docstring), :970-977 (`gate_write` calls `_check_raw_put_grant("gate_write", self._GATE_FIELDS)` before opening the transaction), :915-930 (`_EMBEDDED_DOC_FIELDS`, `_check_raw_put_grant`, `_GATE_FIELDS`). The invariant is pinned by two live tests: archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:253-262 (`test_gate_write_does_not_invalidate_vectors`) and :264-276 (`test_the_raw_put_grant_is_checked_for_the_gate_writer`). Plan §15.7 at ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1028-1034 and §6.4 at :422-440.
findings.proposed_fix: Put the decision in the shared helper so it cannot be got wrong: `_put_fields(txn, key, fields)` computes `touched = fields.keys() & _EMBEDDED_DOC_FIELDS`; if it is non-empty it calls `invalidate_vectors([key])` before the put, otherwise it calls `_check_raw_put_grant`. Then move the grant check off `gate_write()` (where it now guards the wrong thing) onto `update_gate_fields`, drop the "no vector is invalidated" sentence from the class docstring, and keep the existing two tests plus one new one asserting that `put_interpretation` *does* tombstone the vector.

findings.title: D14 invalidates the answer tool's "answered means durable" discipline, and the completeness invariant that marks the theory still tests the in-memory results
findings.claim: The `answer` tool writes to LMDB first and only then sets `task.results[key]`, with an explicit comment that this is what makes "answered" mean "durable"; `interpret_file`'s completeness check then tests `results` and, on the strength of it, `interpret_cone` marks the theory interpreted. Under D14 `on_answer` fills `results[key]` in memory and the store write moves into the gate, so the check no longer proves what its own docstring says it proves — the property now holds only through a three-module argument (a gate that does not write must raise, and every raise fails the TaskGroup). Secondly, the per-item write failure that comment was written for (semantic_interpretation.py:610-623 records the surrogate/msgpack crash it fixed) can no longer be reported back to the agent and re-asked: it now surfaces as a `GateError` that discards the entire theory's paid-for answers.
findings.evidence: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:602-624 ("PERSIST FIRST, MARK IN MEMORY SECOND … This way 'answered' means 'durable'", the per-item `except Exception` that leaves the entry unanswered and returns the reason to the agent) and :1228-1244 ("COMPLETENESS INVARIANT … interpret_cone marks a theory interpreted as soon as interpret' RETURNS", tested as `answered < len(task.entries)`). Plan §15.3 at ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:826 (`self.results[key] = text  # in memory only (D14)`) and §5.4's failure clause at :299-302.
findings.proposed_fix: Two cheap changes that keep D14 intact. (a) Make the final check test durability directly — `all(task.state[i] in (_DONE, _NOT_ENROLLED) for i in range(n))` — instead of `results[i] is not None`, and re-word the invariant comment to say that `_DONE` is what licenses `mark_interpreted`. (b) Validate the answer where the agent can still be told: in `on_answer`, after the existing surrogate strip, `msgpack.packb(trans)` (or the same round trip the codec does) and reject the item through the tool's `errors` list as today, so an unstorable text is still one bad item rather than one dead theory. State in §5.4 that any other step-5 failure discards the theory's LLM work.

findings.title: The resolved prefilter store is parked on the shared `Server` object, which is process-global and never cleared
findings.plan_sections: §15.8 ("Ordering of the startup check's result", lines 1066-1072); §5.6 (lines 383-392); D5, D2
findings.claim: `connection.server.gate_emb_store` puts config-derived, per-run state on an object shared by every connection of the RPC host — one host serves a whole fleet of Isabelle processes, and the package already treats per-connection caching as the rule for anything resolved from a user's context. The slot is written once per cone run and never cleared, so "a missing attribute means not checked ⇒ prefilter skipped" only holds for the first run in the host's life: a later run whose startup check failed (or which never ran one) silently inherits the previous run's provider — resolved from another process's `Semantic_Embedding.embedding_model` and bound to a `Connection` that has since closed. A prefilter under the wrong model is not a safe default: it is the similarity backstop D2 relies on to catch a false "same".
findings.evidence: Plan §15.8 at ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1066-1072. `Server` is created once and handed to every `Connection` (../Isabelle_RPC/Isabelle_RPC_Host/rpc.py:248-271 and :79, `self.server = server` in `Connection.__init__`; `handle_client` at :279-282 builds one `Connection` per client against that one server). The package's own precedent is explicit: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:125-133, "Cached per CONNECTION, not module-level: one RPC host serves a whole fleet of Isabelle processes". D5 is at plan line 56, D2 at line 53.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the server slot and use the per-connection resolution that already exists: `interpret_file` calls `await connection.semantic_vector_store()` (Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:2792-2813, already cached per connection), with `_resolve_embedding_config(warn=False)` per D16, and remembers a failure on its own task (`prefilter_disabled`). §5.6's startup check keeps its single job — printing text §12 #4 once per cone run — and stops carrying an object across connections. This also removes the need for §15.8's "alternative" module-level registry.

findings.title: Crash shape (ii) and its ported test say "nothing written" for an aborted gate write, which stops being true once `put_interpretation` invalidates inside the transaction
findings.claim: `put_interpretation` invalidates vectors first, inside the `gate_write` transaction; the vector stores are separate LMDB environments whose write commits immediately, so an abort of the gate transaction rolls back the record and the counter but leaves the vector tombstones on disk. That is benign and self-healing (the next embed pass refills from the old text, exactly as `__setitem__` documents), but the plan states crash shape (ii) as "nothing written" and §10 asks for a test that an aborted write "leaves store and counter byte-identical" — an assertion the existing step-1 test already makes and that a reviewer extending it to the vector stores would find false.
findings.evidence: Plan §6.4 at ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:449-452 and §10 at :588; §15.7's ordering at :1028-1032. Vector writes commit on their own env: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_embedding.py:1161-1180 (`invalidate_vectors_in_store` opens its own `env.begin(write=True)`), driven per store by :1154-1158. The self-healing rationale is already written down at Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:713-719 (`__setitem__`, "a crash between the two leaves the vector tombstoned and the record still old … wasted work that heals itself"). The current test asserting the strong form is archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:224-238.
findings.proposed_fix: Re-word crash shape (ii) as "the record and the counter are untouched; a vector tombstone written before the abort is a wasted re-embed that heals itself (ordering rule 1, `__setitem__`)", and scope the §10 test to the semantics store and the counter, adding one positive assertion that a *successful* `put_interpretation` tombstoned the key's vector.

accurate: The storage core of the plan is sound and, in several places, better than what it replaces. Putting the mint inside `gate_write` in the same transaction as the record that stores it (§6.3, §5.4 step 5) is exactly the same-transaction rule `counter_next` documents (semantics.py:559-568), and removing the scan-time mint (§15.8 step 2) makes a dry run and a scan genuinely write-free, so no provisional number can ever reach a stored `interpreted_at`. Building the new writers on `backfill_field`'s per-key body (`_raw_for_update` → `_decode` → `_replace` → `_encode` → `txn.put`) rather than on `update_expr`'s positional shape is the right reuse: it keeps copy-up-then-modify over the layered store, preserves fields the wire does not carry (`experience`, `goal_patterns`) that today's `Semantic_DB[key] = SemanticRecord(...)` in `write_answer` silently drops, and handles the absent and tombstoned cases uniformly. Invalidating vectors first inside `put_interpretation` follows ordering rule 1 with `update_expr` as an in-transaction precedent, and separating `update_interpretation` (wire fields, invalidates) from `update_gate_fields` (gate fields, no invalidation) makes D11's "text only" correction expressible without touching a gate field. On the counter invariant: ε taken at write time is the counter's current value and a mint is `counter_next`, while every `interpreted_at` is a max over stored versions, so no stored value can exceed the counter on any path that commits; the snapshot raise runs in its own transaction with no mint and no `await` between the eff* computation and the write, so it cannot pick up an interleaved bump. The crash shapes are argued correctly in substance — an answer in flight leaves nothing on disk and is re-listed by the very criterion that enrolled it, and a cross-theory dependent left stale by an interrupted run is re-listed rather than silently absorbed, because a lower `interpreted_at` is always the conservative direction. Finally, the prefilter's "fresh" document text is byte-identical to the text the entity's real vector will later be built from, so it warms `Embedding_Provider`'s disk cache instead of wasting a call.

findings.title: "tracked" carries three different spellings and two contradictory definitions inside §15.5; `_TRACKED_KINDS` is defined but never used
findings.claim: One predicate — "is this entity gated?" — appears in the blueprint under three spellings, two of which disagree, and the constant introduced for it is never read by any code in §15. §15.1 introduces `_TRACKED_KINDS = (_KIND_CONSTANT, _KIND_TYPE, _KIND_CLASS, _KIND_LOCALE)` "for §5.4 step 1", but §15.5's `_gate` instead writes `tracked = e.semantic_digest is not None` (line 884), and the parenthetical under `_write` (line 946) says `tracked` "becomes `e.semantic_digest is not None or bool(e.deps)` as the scan already uses (:1101)". Under that third definition a theorem-alike entry (digest None, deps present) is `tracked`, so it skips `_write`'s `if not tracked:` branch (line 922, whose own comment says that branch is "theorem-alike (deps present) or persistent") and falls into `elif verdict is None`, which sets `version = w.counter_value()` and `baseline = text`. That stores a `baseline_interpretation` on a theorem-alike record — forbidden by D15, §3 row 4 and §6.1 ("None for theorem-alike") — and resets a theorem-alike's stored version to today's ε, which is strictly larger than the ε it was first written under, so it reads as a mint to its dependents and spuriously re-interprets them. Today's code has exactly the guard this pseudocode drops (semantic_interpretation.py:946-947: `rec.version if rec is not None and rec.version else epsilon`); §15.5's `rec.version` in that branch would also raise AttributeError on a first-written theorem-alike, where `rec is None`.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 884 (`tracked = e.semantic_digest is not None`), 922 (`if not tracked:   # theorem-alike (deps present) or persistent`), 946 (`becomes e.semantic_digest is not None or bool(e.deps)`), 722 (`_TRACKED_KINDS` "the kinds the gate judges"); glossary line 23 defines a tracked entity as a WIP entity of the four name-addressed kinds. Code: semantic_interpretation.py:265-271 (Entry.semantic_digest is None for theorem-alike AND for every persistent-theory entry), :392 (`tracked = version is not None` in write_answer), :946-947 (the None guard), :1101 (`tracked = e.semantic_digest is not None or bool(e.deps)` — the scan's *different* notion, "increment-tracked").
findings.proposed_fix: Fix one name per concept (project rule) and put it on `Entry`, where both the scan and the gate can read it: `Entry.is_gated` = `self.semantic_digest is not None` (equivalently `self.kind in _TRACKED_KINDS and not persistent`, but only one may be the definition) and `Entry.is_increment_tracked` = `self.semantic_digest is not None or bool(self.deps)`. Rewrite §15.5's `_gate`/`_write` to use `e.is_gated` throughout, delete the parenthetical at line 946 (it describes the scan's predicate, not `_write`'s), and either use `_TRACKED_KINDS` inside `is_gated` or drop the constant. Restore the `rec is not None and rec.version` guard in the theorem-alike branch.

findings.title: `JudgeTask` inherits the whole queue/retry machine and fakes three fields to satisfy it; "no verdict" travels as a FatalAgentError through a blanket `except Exception`
findings.claim: The judge needs exactly two things from the interpretation runner: the recycle ladder (usage cap / rate limit / poisoned session / bounded catch-all) and per-turn cost accumulation. The plan gets them by making the judge a full `AgentTask` and then forging the state the queue loop expects: `self.enqueue(0)` in the constructor, `judge.results[key] = args["why"]` written "so the retry loop sees the entry answered", `judge.state[0] = _DONE` set by hand, an `on_answer` implemented as an unused stub, a `retry_report` that returns `""` to suppress a user line the judge must not print, and a new `max_stalled_retries` attribute whose only purpose is to make the interpretation loop's ten-round stall counter mean "one round" for the judge. Worse, the normal outcome "the judge said nothing" is delivered as `FatalAgentError` raised by `_retry_unanswered` (semantic_interpretation.py:784-792) and caught in `_judge` by `except Exception` (§15.5 line 916) — so a genuine bug anywhere in the judge path (a TypeError building the pair prompt, a LookupError in the verdict tool) is silently reinterpreted as CHANGED. This is machinery bent to fit, not machinery reused.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 989 (`self.enqueue(0)`), 992 (`on_answer ... (unused; the verdict tool records directly)`), 993 (`retry_report -> ""`), 995 (`unanswered_failure -> f"judge gave no verdict for {names[0]}"`), 998-1001 (`max_stalled_retries` attribute), 1004-1006 (verdict handler sets `results[key]` and `state[0]`), 913-916 (`_judge` ... `CHANGED otherwise (including FatalAgentError, caught with except Exception)`). Code: semantic_interpretation.py:747-862 (`_run_agent`: the recycle ladder is the only part the judge needs), :784-792 (the stall give-up raises FatalAgentError), :162 (`_MAX_STALLED_RETRIES`). Drivers touch a task only for `model`, `api_retry_errors` and `accumulate_usage` (claude_code.py:266-267, 290-291, 321, 333-334; codex.py:415; interpretation_driver/__init__.py:193-220).
findings.proposed_fix: Split `_run_agent` into the part that is genuinely shared and the part that is not: `async def _with_recycle(make_driver, task, body, depth=0)` keeps today's `async with make_driver() as driver:` plus the five exception handlers verbatim and calls `await body(driver)`; the interpretation queue loop of §15.4 becomes that body for `InterpretationTask`, and the judge's body is three lines (`run_turn(pair_prompt)`; if `judge.verdict is None`, `run_turn(retry_prompt)`; return). Then `AgentTask` holds only what the drivers actually consume — connection, theory identity, driver/model, `api_retry_errors`, the `total_*`/`run_*` accumulators, `historical_cost`/`write_cost`, `cost_prefix` — and the queue, the five states, `results`, `_keys`, `format_entries`, the three retry strings and `max_stalled_retries` all stay in `InterpretationTask`, where they mean something. `JudgeTask` then holds one entry, `verdict`, and nothing else; "no verdict" becomes `judge.verdict is None`, a value rather than an exception, and `_judge` can narrow its `except` to the failure classes that really are failures.

findings.title: `connection.server.gate_emb_store` is a hidden process-global that bypasses the per-connection `Connection.semantic_vector_store()` registry that already exists
findings.claim: The plan resolves the embedding store once on the startup check's connection, stashes it on the shared `Server` object as an ad-hoc attribute, and has `interpret_file` read it back with "a missing attribute means 'not checked'". Three things are wrong with that shape. (i) `Server` is one object for the whole host process, shared by every connection and by unrelated tools, so this is a process-global under a per-connection name. (ii) The convention "attribute absent ⇒ treat as None ⇒ prefilter skipped" is unenforceable and indistinguishable from "the check ran and failed" — precisely the silent-degradation shape D10 forbids elsewhere. (iii) It re-invents a registry that already exists: `Connection.semantic_vector_store()` (semantics.py:2803-2812) is exactly "get or create the Semantic_Vector_Store for the resolved model", cached per connection by `Semantic_Vector_Store.__init__` (semantics.py:1991-1997). Because §5.6 already adds the `Config.lookup` callback to `send_for_interpretation`'s callback list — i.e. to the very connection `interpret_file` runs on — that connection can resolve the store itself, on the user's own context, with no new attribute and no cross-connection object. As written, the store handed to a theory carries `self.connection = <the startup connection>`, so its `_get_reranker`/config lookups would go to a connection that is not the one running the theory.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 1066-1072 ("the startup RPC stores it on the connection's server object for the run (`connection.server.gate_emb_store`) ... a missing attribute means 'not checked' and is treated as None"). Code: rpc.py:73-79 (`Connection.__init__` takes the one shared `server`), semantics.py:2803-2812 (`_conn_semantic_vector_store`, installed as `Connection.semantic_vector_store`), semantics.py:1991-1997 (per-connection, per-model registration with a duplicate raise), semantics.py:2737-2779 (`_resolve_embedding_config(connection)` — the config path §5.6 makes available on the interpret_file connection).
findings.proposed_fix: Drop `gate_emb_store` entirely. Give `InterpretationTask` a lazy accessor that calls `await self.connection.semantic_vector_store()` on first use and caches the result (or `None` after a failure, setting `prefilter_disabled`), so the existing per-connection registry does the caching and the user's own context governs the model (D5). Reduce `Semantic_Store.check_embedding_service` to its remaining, real duty: resolve the config and construct the provider once, before any LLM money is spent, so text §12 #4 is printed once per run and the failure is known early; pass its verdict as a plain per-run flag (module-level, one warn-once boolean of the same shape as claude_code.py:56's `_UNEXPECTED_BILLING_WARNED`) rather than as a smuggled object. If only the provider is wanted, note that `store.emb_provider` is all §5.4 step 2 uses.

findings.title: `Gate_Writer.put_interpretation`'s 13-keyword signature restates the Record field list a third time, and its copy-up-then-modify read is dead
findings.claim: `put_interpretation(key, *, kind, name, expr, interpretation, locale_provenance, theory_constituents, position, from_collection, semantic_digest, deps, version, interpreted_at, baseline_interpretation)` supplies 13 of the Record's 15 fields; the only two it does not supply, `experience` and `goal_patterns`, are `None` for every kind this pipeline writes (EXPERIENCE is excluded from interpretation at semantic_interpretation.py:125-133). So the `_raw_for_update` → `_decode` → `_replace` round trip the plan prescribes preserves nothing, while the parameter list becomes the third place the record's shape is written out (after `Record._fields` and the call site's kwargs) and the fourth thing that has to be kept in step when a field is added — §6.1 already lists four such places for `baseline_interpretation`. Meanwhile `__setitem__` (semantics.py:703-723) is already "invalidate the vectors, then put the record" and differs only in owning its own transaction.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 1028-1034 (the signature and "copy-up-then-modify"), 935-938 (the call site passing all thirteen), 428-440 (§6.4's description). Code: semantics.py:703-723 (`__setitem__`: `invalidate_vectors([key])` then `txn.put(key, self._encode(record))`), :168 (`RECORD_FIELD_COUNT`), semantic_interpretation.py:393-402 (today's `write_answer` already builds the whole `SemanticRecord` literal at the call site).
findings.proposed_fix: Make the gate writer's method take a record: `Gate_Writer.put(key, rec: Record) -> Record` = `invalidate_vectors([key]); txn.put(key, self._db._encode(rec)); return rec`, and re-express `Semantic_DB.__setitem__` as `with self.gate_write() as w: w.put(key, record)` so one body carries the "vectors first" rule for both writers, by shape. The gate call site then keeps today's `SemanticRecord(...)` literal (semantic_interpretation.py:393-402) with the gate fields filled in, and already holds the record it must put into `rec_cache` — no return-value plumbing, no 13-keyword signature, and one fewer place to update at the next codec bump. `update_interpretation` keeps its copy-up read, where it is genuinely needed (it deliberately does not supply the gate fields).

findings.title: `_write` puts a fabricated record into `rec_cache` and repairs it afterwards, so the stated "rec_cache == store" invariant holds only by discipline
findings.claim: §5.4 step 5 states the invariant "on commit the record is put back into `rec_cache` (so 'rec_cache == store' holds for every later eff*)", and then §15.5's `_write` breaks it deliberately: it writes a "provisional record with the new version" into `rec_cache` before the transaction and overwrites it with the written record afterwards. The invariant therefore depends on two paired assignments straddling a fallible write — if `put_interpretation` raises, the cache keeps a record that is not in the store. The fabricated record is also a state that exists nowhere else: new `version` with the *pre-run* `interpreted_at`. That pair is read by `_contrib`'s wall test (semantic_interpretation.py:989-1003) whenever E is reachable from its own dependencies, and the plan never says which reading is intended there. The fabrication exists only because `eff_star(task, e)` is specified to take an entry and read E's own version out of the cache — even though the function it is an extraction of, `eff_value(version, deps)` (semantic_interpretation.py:1084-1090), already takes the version as an argument.
findings.evidence: Plan lines 288-293 (the invariant), 933-939 (`task.rec_cache[e.universal_key] = provisional record with the new version` / `ia = eff_star(task, e)` / `written = w.put_interpretation(...)` / `task.rec_cache[e.universal_key] = written`), 965-971 (`eff_star(task, e)` is "today's `eff_value(version, deps)` closure (:1083)"). Code: semantic_interpretation.py:1084-1090 (`eff_value(version, deps)` takes the version explicitly), :989-1003 (`_contrib` reads `r.version` and `r.interpreted_at` of whatever `rec_cache` holds).
findings.proposed_fix: Keep `_EffStar`'s entry point at today's signature — `eff_star(version, deps)` — and call `ia = task.eff.eff_value(version, e.deps)` with the just-minted version passed in; no record is fabricated, `rec_cache` is assigned exactly once, from the write, and the invariant becomes true by shape rather than by paired assignments. If the cyclic case (E reachable from its own dependencies) is meant to see the new version, say so in one line and express it as an explicit self-override on `_EffStar` (a `{key: version}` argument consulted by `_rec_of`/`_contrib`) instead of a mutation of the shared cache — an override is scoped to the call and cannot survive a failed write.

findings.title: D12's "no limit" on concurrent judge sessions means up to `_BATCH_SIZE` × `max_threads` agent CLI subprocesses alive at once
findings.claim: SPEC RELAXATION PROPOSAL for D12 ("there is no limit on how many judge sessions run at once"). One `answer` tool call may carry a whole batch, and §15.3's `on_answer` starts a gate per entity the moment it arrives, so a single tool call can spawn `_BATCH_SIZE` = 20 judge sessions simultaneously; theories run concurrently under `schedule_dag` at `Multithreading.max_threads ()` (semantic_store.ML:1929), so the process-wide peak is 20 × max_threads fresh agent sessions — on the default driver, that many `claude` CLI subprocesses, each carrying the ~55k-token fixed context D3 measured. On a 16-thread session that is ~320 concurrent subprocesses. The plan itself notes the shape ("the `answer` tool's array submits several entries at once and independent theories run under `schedule_dag` concurrently, so several gates are in flight at a time (D12: no limit)") without bounding it. Nothing else in this pipeline is unbounded: `_MAX_AGENT_RECYCLES`, `_MAX_STALLED_RETRIES` and `_BATCH_SIZE` all exist precisely because an unbounded loop over an external process is how a run becomes unkillable.

That justification holds only when the acquire succeeded. On the `NONE` arm no lock was ever taken, so closing is pure destruction of a live, heartbeat-good pooled connection. D8's contended case is `by aoa` / `_auto_embed`, which is the frequent one — every collision burns one connection and, once the pool is empty, forces a fresh `make_connection ()` round trip (in ephemeral mode, an attached-state revalidation and TCP connect) for the next RPC.
